Appendix A Two phonon analytic structure factors

In Sec. III.2 we compared the long-wavelength and incoherent approximations for the two-phonon final states, for qq within the first BZ. In this appendix we provide the analytic expressions for both approximations.

A.1 Long-wavelength approximation

Here we discuss how we extend the analytic calculations from [25] for the coherent two-phonon structure factor to additional combinations of final state phonon pairs. As in Sec. III.2, we assume a hadrophilic mediator with fd¯=Ad\overline{f_{d}}=A_{d} throughout this appendix. It was shown in [25] that the structure factor separates into harmonic and anharmonic contributions

S⁡(𝐪,ω)=S(harm)​(𝐪,ω)+S(anh)​(𝐪,ω)S({\bf q},\omega)=S^{\mathrm{(harm)}}({\bf q},\omega)+S^{\mathrm{(anh)}}({\bf q},\omega) (56)

which do not interfere at leading order in the long wavelength limit. The first term involves expanding (13) to second order; note that it was referred to as the contact term in [25]. The anharmonic term is computed using an anharmonic phonon interaction Hamiltonian to first order. The specific matrix elements to be used are given in equations (12) and (13) of [25]. We take the long-wavelength approximation for the phonon modes, as described in Sec. III.1. For a crystal with two atoms in the unit cell, the longitudinal eigenvectors can be approximated by

𝐞LA,𝐤,1\displaystyle{\bf e}_{\mathrm{LA,{\bf k},1}} ≈A1A1+A2​𝐤^,\displaystyle\approx\frac{\sqrt{A_{1}}}{\sqrt{A_{1}+A_{2}}}\hat{{\bf k}}, (57)
𝐞LA,𝐤,2\displaystyle{\bf e}_{\mathrm{LA,{\bf k},2}} ≈A2A1+A2e−i𝐤⋅𝐫20𝐤^\displaystyle\approx\frac{\sqrt{A_{2}}}{\sqrt{A_{1}+A_{2}}}e^{-i{\bf k}\cdot{\bf r}_{2}^{0}}\hat{{\bf k}} (58)
𝐞LO,𝐤,1\displaystyle{\bf e}_{\mathrm{LO,{\bf k},1}} ≈A2A1+A2​𝐤^,\displaystyle\approx\frac{\sqrt{A_{2}}}{\sqrt{A_{1}+A_{2}}}\hat{{\bf k}}, (59)
𝐞LO,𝐤,2\displaystyle{\bf e}_{\mathrm{LO,{\bf k},2}} ≈−A1A1+A2e−i𝐤⋅𝐫20𝐤^.\displaystyle\approx-\frac{\sqrt{A_{1}}}{\sqrt{A_{1}+A_{2}}}e^{-i{\bf k}\cdot{\bf r}_{2}^{0}}\hat{{\bf k}}. (60)

with 𝐤^\hat{{\bf k}} the unit vector along the phonon propagation direction. Note that the 𝐫20{\bf r}_{2}^{0} dependence was neglected in the LA eigenvector in (27) and in [25]; here we have kept this additional phase so that the acoustic and optical eigenvectors are explicitly orthogonal across a unit cell. This additional phase factor will only be relevant in cases where there is a destructive interference in the leading coupling to acoustic phonons, which occurs for some final states [13]. The transverse eigenvectors lay in the plane perpendicular to 𝐤^\hat{{\bf k}} and have analogous normalizations.

Analytic expressions for the harmonic structure factor were provided in Ref. [25] for acoustic-acoustic final states only. We require expressions for the optical-optical and optical-acoustic final states as well to perform the comparison with the incoherent approximation. A straightforward application of (16) in [25] to the lowest order in qq gives

Appendix B Impulse approximation

In this section we discuss how to obtain the impulse approximation form of the structure factor, (39) in Sec. III.4. To achieve this we must approximate the tt integral in (37) for large qq. The expression in (37) can be written as

𝒞ℓ​d=1V​e−2​Wd​(𝐪)​∫−∞∞d​t​ef⁡(t).\mathcal{C}_{\boldsymbol{\ell}d}=\frac{1}{V}e^{-2W_{d}(\mathbf{q})}\!\int\displaylimits_{-\infty}^{\infty}\!\!dt\,e^{f(t)}. (70)

with

Re⁡[f⁡(t)]≡q22​md​∫d​ω′​Dd​(ω′)ω′​cos⁡(ω′​t)\displaystyle\mathrm{Re}[f(t)]\equiv\frac{q^{2}}{2m_{d}}\int d\omega^{\prime}\frac{D_{d}(\omega^{\prime})}{\omega^{\prime}}\cos(\omega' t )
Im⁡[f⁡(t)]≡q22​md​∫d​ω′​Dd​(ω′)ω′​sin⁡(ω′​t)−ω​t.\displaystyle\mathrm{Im}[f(t)]\equiv\frac{q^{2}}{2m_{d}}\int d\omega^{\prime}\frac{D_{d}(\omega^{\prime})}{\omega^{\prime}}\sin(\omega' t)-\omega t. (71)

From this, we see there is a global maximum in the real part and a global minimum in the modulus of the imaginary part at t=0t=0. This allows us to perform a steepest-descent expansion about t=0t=0, giving

𝒞ℓ​d≈1V​∫−∞∞d​t​ei​t​(q22​md−ω)−t22​q2​ω¯d2​md,\mathcal{C}_{\boldsymbol{\ell}d}\approx\frac{1}{V}\int\displaylimits_{-\infty}^{\infty}\!\!dt\,e^{it(\frac{q^{2}}{2m_{d}}-\omega)-\frac{t^{2}}{2}\frac{q^{2}\bar{\omega}_{d}}{2m_{d}}}, (72)

where again ω¯d=∫d​ω′​ω′​Dd​(ω′)\bar{\omega}_{d}=\int d\omega^{\prime}\omega^{\prime}D_{d}(\omega^{\prime}). Note that the leading term in the expansion about t=0t=0 cancelled the Debye Waller factor, assuming the form given in (24). Evaluating the above gives

𝒞ℓ​d≈1V​2​πΔd2​e−(ω−q22​md)22​Δd2,\mathcal{C}_{\boldsymbol{\ell}d}\approx\frac{1}{V}\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{\Delta_{d}^{2}}}e^{-\frac{\big(\omega-\frac{q^{2}}{2m_{d}}\big)^{2}}{2\Delta_{d}^{2}}}, (73)

which is the impulse approximation result.

In obtaining this form, we have assumed that any other local maxima in tt gives a subdominant contribution to the t=0t=0 maximum. In particular, aside from the t=0t=0 point, which is a global maximum in Re⁡[f⁡(t)]{\rm Re}[f(t)], there are local maxima in the real part which will generally be near integer multiples of 2​π/ω¯d2\pi/\bar{\omega}_{d}. The leading order contribution from each additional maxima tmaxt_{\mathrm{max}} is given by evaluating the real part in the exponential at the location of the maxima.

This must necessarily be smaller than the t=0t=0 contribution since the following inequality is always satisfied

∫d​ω′​Dd​(ω′)ω′​cos⁡(ω′​tmax)<∫d​ω′​Dd​(ω′)ω′.\int d\omega^{\prime}\frac{D_{d}(\omega^{\prime})}{\omega^{\prime}}\cos(\omega' t_{\rm max} )<\int d\omega^{\prime}\frac{D_{d}(\omega^{\prime})}{\omega^{\prime}}. (74)

Since tmax∼2​π/ω¯dt_{\rm max}\sim 2\pi/\bar{\omega}_{d}, the left hand side will be suppressed by an O⁡(1)O(1) amount due to presence of the cos⁡(ω′​tmax)\cos(\omega' t_{\rm max} ). Then, the contribution from the local maxima will be exponentially suppressed:

eq22​md​∫d​ω′​Dd​(ω′)ω′​cos⁡(ω′​tmax)≪eq22​md​∫d​ω′​Dd​(ω′)ω′e^{\frac{q^{2}}{2m_{d}}\int d\omega^{\prime}\frac{D_{d}(\omega^{\prime})}{\omega^{\prime}}\cos(\omega' t_{\rm max})}\ll e^{\frac{q^{2}}{2m_{d}}\int d\omega^{\prime}\frac{D_{d}(\omega^{\prime})}{\omega^{\prime}}} (75)

as long as the following condition is satisfied

q22​md≫1∫d​ω′​Dd​(ω′)ω′∼ω¯d.\frac{q^{2}}{2m_{d}}\gg\frac{1}{\int d\omega^{\prime}\frac{D_{d}(\omega^{\prime})}{\omega^{\prime}}}\sim\bar{\omega}_{d}. (76)

Here we have taken ∫d​ω′​Dd​(ω′)ω′∼1/ω¯d\int d\omega^{\prime}\frac{D_{d}(\omega^{\prime})}{\omega^{\prime}}\sim 1/\bar{\omega}_{d} as a typical scale for this integral, although it will differ by an O⁡(1)O(1) factor. Therefore, as long as the free nuclear recoil energy ω=q2/(2​md)\omega=q^{2}/(2m_{d}) is well above the typical phonon energy ω¯d\bar{\omega}_{d} for a scattering off of atom dd, the t=0t=0 maximum is dominant and the impulse approximation should be accurate.

In the regime where q2/2​mdq^{2}/2m_{d} is comparable to ω¯d\bar{\omega}_{d}, the contributions from the additional maxima in tt can become important. Nevertheless, the impulse approximation is still accurate at large ω\omega even in this case because of cancellations from the rapidly changing phase in Im⁡[f⁡(t)]{\rm Im}[f(t)]. When ω≫ω¯d\omega\gg\bar{\omega}_{d}, then Im⁡[f⁡(t)]≈−ω​t{\rm Im}[f(t)]\approx-\omega t for tt around tmax∼2​π/ω¯dt_{\rm max}\sim 2\pi/\bar{\omega}_{d}. This implies large oscillations of f⁡(t)f(t) around tmaxt_{\rm max}, which suppresses the contribution from these local maxima. On the other hand, if ω≲ω¯d\omega\lesssim\bar{\omega}_{d}, there may be large corrections to the impulse approximation due to these additional maxima.

These effects were shown in Fig. 5a when comparing the multiphonon expansion result to the impulse approximation. The middle panel showed the result if q=2​md​ω¯dq=\sqrt{2m_{d}\bar{\omega}_{d}}, in the mGa≈mAsm_{\text{Ga}}\approx m_{\text{As}} approximation. For ω≳ω¯d\omega\gtrsim\bar{\omega}_{d} the structure factor falls smoothly and can be reasonably captured by the impulse approximation, while for ω≲ω¯d≈22\omega\lesssim\bar{\omega}_{d}\approx 22 meV or at the optical phonon energies 3131 and 3333 meV there are sharp peaks in the multiphonon response that are not captured by the impulse approximation. For q=2​2​md​ω¯dq=2\sqrt{2m_{d}\bar{\omega}_{d}} the many multiphonon peaks merge and add up to a shape similar to the impulse approximation over the whole ω\omega range. Practically, for our calculations, we use the impulse approximation for the structure factor at q>2​2​md​ω¯dq>2\sqrt{2m_{d}\bar{\omega}_{d}}. Though the approximation has small differences with the exact result when q∼2​2​md​ω¯dq\sim 2\sqrt{2m_{d}\bar{\omega}_{d}}, integrating over the allowed phase space for the rate largely washes out these differences.

Appendix C Implementation in DarkELF

In the main text, we presented the formulas in the manner which is most clear from the point of view of the various approximations and their regimes of validity. These formulas were not always suitable however for an efficient numerical implementation, which we address in this section. We also provide details on their implementation in the DarkELF package [29].

In the main text we gave the rate in the isotropic limit, (45). In order to calculate the rate for any mediator and to obtain the differential rate d​R/d​ωdR/d\omega, it is convenient to perform the vv-integral first and rewrite the rate as:

R=14​π​ρT​ρχmχ​σpμχ2​∫ωthω+d​ω​∫q−q+d​q​q​|F~​(q)|2​S​(q,ω)​η​(vmin​(q,ω))R=\frac{1}{4\pi\rho_{T}}\frac{\rho_{\chi}}{m_{\chi}}\frac{\sigma_{p}}{\mu_{\chi}^{2}}\int\displaylimits_{\omega_{\mathrm{th}}}^{\omega_{+}}\!d\omega\,\int\displaylimits_{q_{-}}^{q_{+}}\!dq\,q\,|\tilde{F}(q)|^{2}S(q,\omega)\,\eta(v_{\rm min}(q,\omega)) (77)

where now the integration limits are given by

q±\displaystyle q_{\pm} =mχ​(vmax±vmax2−2​ωmχ)\displaystyle=m_{\chi}\big(v_{\mathrm{max}}\pm\sqrt{v_{\mathrm{max}}^{2}-\frac{2\omega}{m_{\chi}}}\big) (78)
ω+\displaystyle\omega_{+} =12​mχ​vmax2\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}m_{\chi}v_{\rm max}^{2} (79)

with vmax=vesc+vev_{\rm max}=v_{\rm esc}+v_{e} the maximum DM speed in the lab frame. The η\eta function is given by

η⁡(vmin)=∫d3​𝐯​f⁡(𝐯)v​Θ​(v−vmin)\eta(v_{\mathrm{min}})=\int d^{3}\mathbf{v}\frac{f(\mathbf{v})}{v}\Theta(v-v_{\mathrm{min}}) (80)

with vmin​(q,ω)=q2​mχ+ωq.v_{\mathrm{min}}(q,\omega)=\frac{q}{2m_{\chi}}+\frac{\omega}{q}.

To evaluate the rate using incoherent approximation, we provide look-up tables for the structure factor. At each nn for the sum in (36), the qq and ω\omega parts of the integral are separable, so we can capture the ω\omega-dependent part with the family of functions

Fn,d​(ω)≡1n!​(∏i=1n∫d​ωi​Dd​(ωi)ωi)​δ​(∑iωi−ω),F_{n,d}(\omega)\equiv\frac{1}{n!}\left(\prod\displaylimits_{i=1}^{n}\int d\omega_{i}\frac{D_{d}(\omega_{i})}{\omega_{i}}\right)\delta\left(\sum_{i}\omega_{i}-\omega\right), (81)

and calculate the rate in terms of functions Fn,dF_{n,d}. These functions are simple to calculate numerically up to n≤10n\leq 10, which we have tabulated and provided in DarkELF as look-up tables to speed up the calculation. The combination ω¯n​Fn​(ω)\bar{\omega}^{n}F_{n}(\omega) is shown in Fig. 11 for GaAs in the mGa≈mAsm_{\mathrm{Ga}}\approx m_{\mathrm{As}} approximation. For increasingly high nn, the Fn,dF_{n,d} become increasingly smooth.

We have added several additional functions to DarkELF for the differential and integrated rate calculations from the single phonon to the nuclear recoil regime. Tab. 1 describes some of the new relevant functions. These functions currently work for materials with up to two atoms per unit cell. We have included the necessary data files for the multiphonon calculation for GaN, Al, ZnS, GaAs, Si, and Ge from a combination of DFT and experimental sources. We also allow the user to input their own calculations or extractions of the (partial) density of states, as well as momentum-dependent dark matter-nucleon couplings. Before calculating multiphonon scattering rates in DarkELF, it is necessary to tabulate the auxiliary function (81) for each atom. This is done using the DarkELF function create_Fn_omega. This step is the most time consuming part of the calculation, so we provide these pre-tabulated for the aforementioned materials. For calculations with a user-supplied (partial) density of states, these tables must first be updated by running create_Fn_omega. DarkELF will save these new look-up tables for future computations, such that this step only need to be performed once. Next we describe the functions that return important results. All of the following straightforwardly apply equations (77-80).

R_single_phonon: This function takes the energy threshold and DM-nucleon cross sections and outputs the rate in the long-wavelength single phonon regime using the analytic functions (30-31).

R_multiphonons_no_single: This function takes the energy threshold and DM-nucleon cross section as inputs and calculates the total integrated rate, excluding the single phonon processes at long wavelengths q<qBZq<q_{\mathrm{BZ}}. In other words, this calculation includes only the purple (multiphonon expansion) and red (impulse approximation) phase space regions in Fig. 6.

sigma_multiphonons: This takes the energy threshold as input and returns the necessary DM-nucleon cross section to produce three events per kg-year for any number of phonons. In order to return this cross section, this function first calculates the total rate by summing the outputs of R_single_phonon and R_multiphonons_no_single, so it includes the entire calculation scheme depicted in Fig. 6.

_dR_domega_multiphonons_no_single: This function takes the energy transfer ω\omega and DM-nucleon cross section and returns the differential rate d​Rd​ω\frac{dR}{d\omega} at that energy excluding single phonons in the long wavelength regime. This comes from equation (77) without evaluating the ω\omega integral. We exclude the single coherent phonon here since the long-wavelength approximation has delta functions in energy in the differential rate.

Appendix D Additional results

Here, we provide additional results for Ge, Si, and diamond. Concretely, Fig. 12 shows the density of states for these three materials, as extracted from [35]. Fig. 13 shows the differential scattering rate via a massive scalar mediator for two example DM masses in GaAs, Ge and Si targets. Finally, Figs. 14, 15, and 16 are the cross section plots corresponding to an integrated rate of 3 events/kg-year for Ge, Si, and diamond, respectively. The electron recoil cross sections shown (dashed black lines) are based on calculations in [39] for Ge, Si and in [43] for diamond.
